activity.title: I won a MacBook Neo At Salesforce ’s FutureForce Tech Accelerator today, participants were split into 4-5 person groups to pitch, Shark Tank style, to 3 Senior Salesforce Sharks. My team pitched a Dynamic Trust Layer for AI Agents that could, in real time, manage agent identity credentials and permissions in order to maximize autonomy while mitigating risk. Our ask was $5M for 10% of our company. A $50M valuation. Ambitious, but our real target was a $20M valuation. We were last to go. Team after team pitched their ideas, none going anywhere near or above a $5M valuation. Rightfully my team got antsy. “What if we don’t get a deal?” “Are we overpriced? We should lower our valuation.” But I thought otherwise. Having taken a negotiation class out of curiosity my freshman year of college, I knew the importance of anchoring high. So I asked my team to put their trust in me, and hold steady on our valuation. Our turn came. The sharks weren’t biting. Our valuation was indeed much too high. However, this gave us room to negotiate. Eventually, we haggled down to an ask of $5M for 20%, splitting our valuation in half to $25M, and yet still sitting above our fair value estimate. The result? A brand new MacBook Neo. Lesson learned: Go big. Sure, this wasn’t a “real” pitch competition, but when everyone else went left, we went right, and were rewarded for taking the greater risk. Is it time for to pitch my B2B AI SaaS company to YC?? I’m wallin????? ...more

The email in this screenshot isn’t the point. The point is when it arrived. Recruiting for next summer is already moving. While many people are waiting for the fall semester to start, others have been preparing for months. That means: - Practicing LeetCode consistently. - Learning system design. - Building projects that you’re genuinely proud of. - Reaching out to recruiters and engineers. - Refining your resume. - Applying before everyone else does. None of this happened overnight. The work started early. If you’re hoping to land an internship or full-time role next year, don’t wait until classes begin. By then, many companies have already started interviewing, or even extending offers. Start today. And if you’re not sure where to begin or have questions about recruiting, applications, interview prep, or networking, my DMs are open. I’m happy to share anything that helped me. ...more

Autocomplete smoothed out my brain.. I’m currently working on the infamous Malloc Lab in CMU’s 15213 - Intro to computer systems. The goal of the lab is to implement our own dynamic memory allocator, which should have malloc, calloc, realloc, etc. The course asks us to turn off autocomplete for the sake of academic integrity, which forced me to really write code manually for the first time in even longer than agentic coding has been around. I don’t even have tab complete for function names.. But lo and behold, I UNDERSTAND IT NOW It allows me to practice thinking critically about the choices I make in my design and their tradeoffs, which is exactly the kind of skills engineers need in this ever evolving industry. It’s also more fun now because I have full control over MY OWN solution, not just the highest probability one based on all the training examples a model saw. Cooper Bruno is my witness🙏🏿 ...more

Tolu Oshin earned a combined bachelor’s in computer engineering and master’s in computer science from Michigan State University in four years, interned at General Motors and then Microsoft , and is now full-time at Two Sigma . He talks about the challenges he faced with technical interviews early on, and how he built his way up gradually through exposure to different kinds of problems, more reps, and a shift in how he prepared. If you’re early in your journey and interviews aren’t clicking yet, this is a useful one. Full conversation on YouTube (link in comments).

As I wrap up my summer internship with Ford Motor Company , I’m incredibly grateful for the people, experiences, and opportunities that made this summer so valuable. Over the past 12 weeks, I had the opportunity to work alongside engineers across multiple teams and contribute to projects involving engineering quality, digital tools, and process improvement. Some of the highlights from my summer included: • Developing an AI assistant to support Failure Mode Avoidance and reduce engineering downtime. • Gaining firsthand experience with engineering quality and review through audits across vehicle programs. • Improving internal tools and workflows using Power BI and Power Apps. • Experiencing Ford beyond my day-to-day work through plant tours, prototype builds, testing facilities, and immersive vehicle experiences. Just as valuable as the work were the people I learned from throughout the summer. A special thank you to my manager, Nathan Wieseler , for his mentorship, guidance, and for trusting me with meaningful work. I’m also thankful to my teammates, mentors, and fellow interns who made this such a great experience. I’m proud of what I was able to contribute and excited to take everything I learned with me as I head back to Carnegie Mellon. #FordIntern #WeAreFord

My best friend got married last week. And it hit me harder than I expected. I met Arhum in college. We did everything together back then. Classes, food runs, late nights, all of it. Then we graduated. Then we got jobs. Then life got busy. Now, all of a sudden, he's starting a family of his own. And while I am happy for him, this also means our random hangouts are done. It's a bittersweet moment as a friend. At 18, the average American spends about 2 hours a day with friends. By 25 it is one hour. By 30 it is 46 minutes. Nobody warns you about that drop. It happens slowly, while everyone is busy building a career and a family. So that means you have to intentionally make time for friends. Be the guy that texts first. Be the guy that calls for no reason. Be the guy that books the flight. Be the guy that keeps showing up. And do not wait until you are less busy. You will NEVER be less busy. Congrats Arhum. Watching you build this life has been one of the best parts of mine. ♻️ Repost this if there is someone you have been meaning to call.
